title: Writing for agents
bridge: Writing a skill is like writing a PR description for a reviewer from the other team. The goal comes first, then why, where to look and what proves it. Except this reader follows the text on every task, literally. So every rule costs attention on every run, and a wrong rule is followed anyway.
intro: Four rhino-core texts shape how people and Nova work: plan-and-grill, verify, pr-story and the checking guide. This lesson is about the voice they share: goals, reasons, examples and signs to look deeper, in calm words. It also shows how STYLE.md, the catalog and a monthly rule diet keep that voice short and honest.

picture.caption: One style guide shapes four texts; people and Nova follow them from plan to PR; the rule diet keeps them short.

sections.h: Two ways to write the same rule
p: Read the two versions below. The first is a list of orders in capitals. The second says what we want, why, where to start, and what to do when something fails.

Strong models follow the first one too well. They run every test on a typo fix, and they cannot judge a case the rule never named. G8-05 puts it plainly: hard rules about method make strong models worse, while goals, reasons and examples work better.
The second version also tells a person what to do. People and Nova read the same skills, so one good text serves both.
sections.because: We give the reason with every instruction, because a reader who knows why can handle the case the text never mentioned.

code.file: a rule, before and after (lab text)
code.text:
<!-- Before: an order with no reason -->
YOU MUST ALWAYS RUN ALL THE TESTS BEFORE YOU COMMIT. NEVER SKIP THIS STEP.
IMPORTANT: DO NOT DELETE TESTS.

<!-- After: a goal, a reason, a place to start, and what to do when it fails -->
## Before you say done
Goal: the reviewer can see the change works without running it themselves.
Start with the area's verify command (references/per-area.md). It runs lint, types and the
related tests, which is enough for most changes and takes minutes, not the whole suite.
Look deeper when you changed a serializer, a migration or shared UI.
If a check fails, it is yours until main's latest run fails the same way; then link that run.
Fix the code rather than the test. If you think the test is wrong, say why in the PR.

notes.text: Capitals and ALWAYS: the reader cannot tell what matters, or what to do when it cannot comply.
A real wall written as a shout. Walls belong in hooks and checks (lesson p11-3), not in prose.
The goal first, in terms of the reviewer: what should be true when we are done.
Where to start, with a pointer to the file that has the exact commands.
The reason it is enough: what it covers and what it costs.
A sign to look deeper. Signs let the reader judge when the default is not enough.
The failure case, with the exact way to show a failure is not yours.
What to do instead of weakening a test, and who decides.

sections.h: STYLE.md, the catalog and the rule diet
p: G8-05 writes STYLE.md in RhinoHealth/claude-plugins. The first line of a skill says when to use it. The body has goals, reasons, examples and signs to look deeper, in calm words, with no ALL-CAPS MUST or CRITICAL. Walls live in hooks and infrastructure, not in prompts.
It also sets sizes and habits. Prefer a CLI over an MCP server, and give an agent 5 to 10 skills. Keep SKILL.md short with references/ for depth, and write evals before long instructions.

catalog.yaml names each shared skill's plugin and owner, and the owner keeps its evals green. Plugin CI fails a PR that adds a skill missing from the catalog or with fewer than 3 eval cases. On the first Monday of each month, each owner opens a rule-diet PR. It removes one rule, runs the evals with and without it, and keeps the removal if scores hold.
sections.because: We give every skill an owner in one file, because a skill nobody owns is a skill whose evals nobody fixes.

notes.text: The file's purpose in one line, so nobody has to guess what it is for.
Owners keep their skill's evals green and run its monthly rule diet.
CI reads this file and compares it with the skills folders in the plugins.
Platform has no GitHub team yet, so Slack is the way to reach it.
Guild owners are GitHub teams, so a review request reaches the whole guild.
Security is an owner too, for security-fix.
Each skill names its plugin and its owner.
A skill can have two owners when two teams depend on it.

p: verify (G8-04) is the skill for any code change before saying done. Its goal is proof a reviewer can see: each check ran, and it could have failed. People, Nova and every routine use it, so done means the same thing everywhere.

Read how the body is built. Where to start names the commands. Signs to look deeper name the changes that need more. Prove a check can fail turns a habit into one concrete action. When a check fails gives the honest path, not the cheap one.

One line in fcp's frontend/AGENTS.md and the root CLAUDE.md points at it. It reads: 'Before you say a change is done, use the verify skill (rhino-core)'. npm run verify and poe verify do not exist yet. G7 adds them, and references/per-area.md lists the commands to run until then.
sections.because: We name signs to look deeper instead of a checklist per file type, because the reader can then judge changes nobody listed.

code.text:
# verify: proof, not claims

## Where to start
Run the area's verify command (references/per-area.md): `npm run verify` in frontend/, `poe verify` for cloud,
client and sdk. Then check what the user would see: open the flow in FCP Lab with seed data (fcp-lab skill), or
call the API and read the response.

## Signs to look deeper
You changed a serializer, a migration, a proto, a public SDK function or shared UI; there is no test near the
diff; the change is about timing, permissions or time zones.

## Prove a check can fail
Plant a small bug in your change (flip a condition), run the check, watch it fail, revert. If it still passes,
the check doesn't cover your change: write a better one.

## When a check fails
It's yours until main's latest run shows the same failure; then link that run and say so. The answer is to fix
the code, not to skip, delete or loosen the check. If you think a test is wrong, explain why in the PR and leave
the call to the reviewer.

## Record the proof
Per check: the command, pass or fail, and the proof the plan named (a video up to 30 s, screenshots at 760 and
1440, or text). Seed data only.

notes.text: The title states the goal in three words.
Exact commands, and a pointer to the file with the per-area details.
What the user would see is part of the check, not an extra.
Signs, not rules: each one is a reason to go deeper.
Planting a bug proves the check covers the change. A check that cannot fail proves nothing.
Whose failure is it? The answer is evidence: main's latest run.
The cheap path, named and closed, with the reason in the same sentence.
Proof per check, in the form the plan named, with seed data only.

sections.h: The checking guide: where to start
p: G4-08 adds references/checking-guide.md to the verify skill. Per kind of change it gives a place to start, the signs to look deeper, and the proof that fits. The plan has eight kinds, from docs to dependency bumps; the sketch shows three.

It uses commands that exist today, such as npm run lint, npm run check-types and ./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh. It says plainly which tools are not in fcp yet, and what to do until they land. A guide that names a missing command sends the reader into a wall.

Its 3 eval cases check the depth, not the words. They are a CSS-only change, a shared component on many pages, and a serializer field rename. Nova should start small on the first and go deeper on the other two.
sections.because: We write start, look deeper and proof per kind, because a typo and a risky change need different checking.

code.text:
<!-- rhino-core/skills/verify/references/checking-guide.md in RhinoHealth/claude-plugins (path per G8's layout; confirm) -->
# Checking guide: where to start, when to look deeper

A starting point, not a rulebook or a timetable. Start from what fits the change, go deeper whenever you see
a reason, and take the time that needs. In the PR, say what you checked, why, and what you chose not to check.

## FE component
- Start: `npm run lint`, `npm run check-types`, the related vitest files, the component's stories in each screen state.
- Look deeper when many pages use it or the layout changes: open those pages at 760 and 1440 (e2e/helpers/responsive.ts).
- Proof: assertions on visible text and ARIA roles; a short video per QA check.

## FE page flow
- Start: the above, plus the Playwright spec for that flow (frontend/e2e/pr/*.spec.ts) on FCP Lab with seed data.
- Look deeper when it touches permissions, data loading or forms: run the neighbouring specs, try the edge cases by hand.
- Proof: the specs ran, a video per check, the Playwright trace.

## BE logic
- Start: pre-commit on the changed files, then `./scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.tests.<module>`.
- Look deeper when the code is shared, checks permissions, or queries in a loop: run the wider suite and count queries.
- Proof: a new test that failed before the fix and passes after.

## When a check fails
Never weaken it. If main fails the same way, link main's run and say so. A flaky test gets flagged with evidence.

notes.text: Where the file lives. The path follows G8's layout; the ticket says to confirm it.
It says what it is not: a rulebook or a timetable. Take the time the change needs.
The PR says what was checked, why, and what was left out on purpose.
Start: the cheap checks that fit a component.
Look deeper: the condition, then the action, with the real helper file for the two widths.
Proof: what kind of evidence fits this kind of change.
The BE start uses the real script and module path that exist in fcp today.
The failure rule, the same as in verify, in one calm line.

sections.h: pr-story: the same headings every time
p: Anyone may review any area, so every PR must be readable by someone from the other team in a few minutes. pr-story (G8-06) fixes the headings and their order. fcp's .github/pull_request_template.md moves to the same headings, so there is never a second template.

It also says when to add media. A video of up to 30 seconds for flows, and screenshots at 760 and 1440 for layout. A diagram for a changed flow between services, and text for API calls and migrations. Nothing for refactors. Never pictures of code or logs, never real data.

Nova's PR body comes from the same headings. G4-20's pr-body.ts renders them from the evidence pack and always ends with Requested-by: @<login>. It keeps ### References with the Jira link, so add-jira-links.yml leaves the body alone.
sections.because: We fix the headings, because a reviewer who knows where proof sits finds it in seconds on any PR.

code.text:
# pr-story

A reviewer from the other team should understand this PR in two minutes. Same headings, same order, every time.
Keep the part above the fold under about 300 words; link long output instead of pasting it.

Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).

## What changes
1-3 plain sentences about the visible effect.
## Why
The ticket link, and the root cause in one line with file:line.
## How it was checked
Each check from the plan: pass or fail, with its proof labelled by check.
## What was not checked, and why
## Risk and rollback
The risk, how to revert, what to watch after merge.
## Where to look first
2-3 files, and any question for the reviewer.
<details><summary>Receipt, trace and cost</summary>Self-review receipt, trace link, harness suggestions, cost and time.</details>

Pick media with references/media.md. Never pictures of code or logs, never real data.

notes.text: The goal in terms of the reader: someone from the other team, two minutes.
Above the fold stays short. Long output is linked, never pasted.
The title format fcp already uses, so history stays searchable.
The visible effect first, in plain sentences.
The root cause with file:line, so a reviewer can jump to it.
Each check from the plan, with its proof labelled by check.
What was not checked is a heading of its own. Honest gaps are part of the story.
The receipt, trace and cost fold away, so they do not push the story down.

sections.h: Link, do not paste; one action per line
p: Pages for agents point at code by path, like file:line, instead of pasting it. Pasted code goes stale the day someone changes the file. A path is read fresh every time.
Runbooks and step lists use one action per line, in order, each with what you should see. A tired person and a model both follow steps better than paragraphs.

Keep walls out of the prose. If something must never happen, a hook, the broker, a ruleset or a required check enforces it. The skill can explain the wall and its reason, so the reader is not surprised when it holds.

callout.text: A sentence in a skill is guidance. Agents never merge, apply, destroy, sync or dispatch because infrastructure stops them, not because a skill asks nicely.

---
name: run-tests
description: "Testing skill."
---
# run-tests

YOU MUST ALWAYS RUN ALL THE TESTS BEFORE YOU COMMIT. NEVER SKIP THIS STEP.
IMPORTANT: DO NOT DELETE TESTS.

Save this checker, a lab version of G8-07's check_skills.py, as check_skill.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lab version of G8-07's skill checks: frontmatter, the when-to-use line and loud words."""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LOUD = re.compile(r"\b(MUST|NEVER|ALWAYS|CRITICAL|IMPORTANT)\b")


def check(path: Path) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    text = path.read_text()
    front, _, body = text.partition("\n---\n")
    if not text.startswith("---\n") or not body:
        return [f"{path}: no frontmatter"], []
    fields = dict(line.split(":", 1) for line in front.splitlines()[1:] if ":" in line and not line.startswith(" "))
    errors, warnings = [], []
    if fields.get("name", "").strip() != path.parent.name:
        errors.append(f"{path}: name does not match the folder {path.parent.name}")
    about = fields.get("description", "") + fields.get("when_to_use", "")
    if len(about) > 600:
        errors.append(f"{path}: description + when_to_use has {len(about)} characters (limit 600)")
    if not re.search(r"\buse (when|before|for)\b", about, re.I):
        errors.append(f"{path}: the description does not say when to use the skill")
    warnings += [f"{path}:{n}: loud words; give a reason instead" for n, line in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1) if LOUD.search(line)]
    return errors, warnings


results = [check(Path(arg)) for arg in sys.argv[1:]]
for errors, warnings in results:
    print("\n".join(["ERROR " + e for e in errors] + ["warn  " + w for w in warnings]) or "ok")
sys.exit(1 if any(errors for errors, _ in results) else 0)

quiz.q: A skill says 'YOU MUST RUN ALL TESTS BEFORE COMMITTING.' What does STYLE.md suggest instead?

options.text: Make it stronger with CRITICAL so the model takes it seriously
options.why: Loud words make strong models over-apply the rule; STYLE.md bans them.

options.text: State the goal and the reason, where to start, and signs to look deeper
options.why: A reader who knows why can judge the cases the text never named.

options.text: Delete it and trust the model
options.why: The habit matters; it needs a reason and a starting point, not deletion.

quiz.q: Why does a page for agents link code by path instead of pasting it?

options.text: Because pasted code goes stale when the file changes, while a path is read fresh
options.why: file:line points at the current code every time.

options.text: Because models cannot read code blocks in Markdown
options.why: They can; the problem is that the copy drifts from the real file.

options.text: Because pasting code breaks the plugin validator
options.why: The validator does not look at code blocks.

quiz.q: In the monthly rule diet, an owner removes one rule and the evals hold. What happens?

options.text: The rule goes back anyway, because rules are safer than no rules
options.why: The diet keeps a removal when scores hold; fewer rules cost less attention.

options.text: The skill's owner must ask Security
options.why: Security owns walls, not guidance; the diet is the skill owner's call.

options.text: The removal is kept: the rule was costing attention without helping
options.why: G8-05: run the evals with and without it, keep the removal if scores hold.
